sources: Monaghan, Patricia. The Encyclopedia of Celtic Mythology and Folklore. Checkmark Books, 2008.
text: Searbhan, also called Sharvon the Surly or Sharvan, was an Irish hero. He appears in the romantic tale of Gráinne and Diarmait. He was a giant and a magician. He helped the fleeing lovers by hiding them in his magical rowan tree. He warned them not to eat the berries, but Gráinne still craved the fruit. Diarmait killed Searbhan so that they could eat it. The giant's dying screams exposed the couple's hiding place to Fionn mac Cumhaill, who was chasing them.
